bib.title: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge

question: Can a model improve its own judging ability, not just its responses, by judging its own judgements, and does that sustain self-improvement beyond Self-Rewarding saturation?
hypothesis: Self-Rewarding saturates or reward-hacks because only the actor, not the judge, is trained; training the judge via a meta-judge should sustain improvement.
contributions: Meta-Rewarding: add an LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge role that scores judgements and yields judge preference pairs
A length-control mechanism for actor preference selection against length explosion
Evidence of gains on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench and in judge agreement with GPT-4 and humans

method.summary: One model plays actor, judge and meta-judge. Per iteration: sample K=7 responses per prompt, score each with N=11 judgments (averaged), build actor pairs with length control; pick the highest-score-variance response, compare judgment pairs with the meta-judge in both orders, rank by Elo and take top/bottom as judge pairs; train DPO on both pair sets. Judge pairs only in iterations 1 and 2.
method.task: iterative self-improving preference optimisation (instruction following and judging)

datasets.name: Evaluation Fine-Tuning (EFT) dataset
datasets.source: Yuan et al. 2024c, built from Open Assistant (Kopf et al. 2024); ranked human responses as LLM-as-a-Judge data

datasets.name: Seed prompt set
datasets.source: Yuan et al. 2024c; generated by Llama-2-70B-Chat with an 8-shot prompt
datasets.preprocessing: identical responses filtered (typically no more than 50 duplicates)

datasets.name: GPT-4 chosen pairs
datasets.source: two seed-model responses per prompt, gpt-4-1106-preview labels, kept when both position orders agree

models.name: Meta-Rewarding M1-M4
models.init_from: SFT on EFT, then each iteration from the previous

other.use: benchmark judge and proxy truth for judge agreement

training.objective: DPO on actor pairs (and judge pairs in iterations 1-2), beta = 0.1
training.epochs: 10 epochs for DPO and SFT, checkpoint selected per iteration

other.sft: 10 epochs, lr 5e-8, batch 32, cosine, epoch 5 checkpoint chosen
other.actor_length_filter: iter 1 drops pairs with chosen response over 2500 characters
other.checkpoints: Meta-Rewarding epoch 6, 4, 2, 2 for iters 1-4; Self-Rewarding epoch 5, 1, 2, 2
other.iterations: Iter 3 and 4 train on actor pairs only
other.note: Table 4 shows Meta-Rewarding iter 4 rho values 0, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4; text says 0.4 used

inference.samples: K = 7 responses per prompt; N = 11 judgments per response (footnote chose 11 from early experiments)
inference.prompting: pointwise 5-point additive judge prompt; pairwise meta-judge prompt run in both position orders

metrics.name: Judge agreement (with and without ties)
metrics.definition: agreement of model-judge ranking with GPT-4 or human preference; ties count 0.5, or are removed

metrics.name: Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: ranking correlation with human ranks averaged over prompts

eval.protocol: GPT-4 as judge on benchmarks; single run per setting, no seeds or significance tests stated beyond Arena-Hard 95% CI

prompts.text: Review the user's question and the corresponding response using the additive 5-point scoring system described below. ... Conclude with the score using the format: "Score: <total points>"

Review the user's question and the corresponding response, along with two judgments. Determine which judgment is more accurate according to the rubric ... Conclude with a clear statement of which judgment is better using the format: "Winner: [Judgement A | Judgement B]"

results.note: Footnote 3: their own evaluation of the seed gives 24.57% LC, probably a different inference template.
results.quote: a win rate improvement of Llama-3-8B-Instruct from 22.9% to 39.4%

results.setup: AlpacaEval 2, 805 prompts, GPT-4-Turbo judge, Llama-3-8B-Instruct seed, 4 iterations, 5,000 prompts per iteration; Self-Rewarding baseline with the same length control
results.table: Table 1, row Self-Rewarding LLM + LC Iteration 4, column LC win rate

results.claim: At iteration 3 Meta-Rewarding LC (35.45) is only 0.58 above Self-Rewarding+LC (34.87); the gap widens to about 4 points at iteration 4.
results.setup: AlpacaEval 2, 805 prompts, GPT-4-Turbo judge, Llama-3-8B-Instruct seed, 4 iterations, 5,000 prompts per iteration
results.table: Table 1, row Meta-Rewarding LLM Iteration 3, column LC win rate

limits: 5-point scoring yields many ties and saturates; responses approach the max score (authors concede)
Meta-judge positional bias persists and hindered iteration 3; judge learns to assign higher scores
Judge shows limited improvement on non-self-generated (human) responses; human correlation gain not sustained over later iterations
Meta-judge also has length bias, needing a judgment-length filter
Judge training only in iterations 1-2; iterations 3-4 are actor-only, so later gains are not judge-training gains directly
Single 8B model, one seed model, no seeds or confidence intervals for AlpacaEval; rho and checkpoints tuned per iteration
Evaluation relies on GPT-4 judges; no human evaluation of responses
Judge agreement at iteration 4 is close between Meta- and Self-Rewarding (79.33 vs 78.42)

terms.definition: the model evaluates its own judgements, comparing two judgements of one response
